Dr Stent

By: Mart-Marie Faure | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
What they thought would be a routine medical check up turned into a nightmare . Three patients share their stories.

Unique Selling Point:
A Young cardiologist with a booming practice in a Durban hospital had colleagues and hospital staff baffled at the amount of angiograms that he was performing on patients, sometimes into the early hours of the morning. They raised concerns with hospital management and were told that they were professionally jealous . Doing some investigation it was established that some of the procedures performed such as inserting stents were unnecessary and healthy arteries were stented.
Patients went for second opinions. it was confirmed that stents were not needed. All three our case studies have developed serious health issues.

Summary:
The doctor qualified as a cardiologist in 2021 from Sefako Makgato hospital in Garankuwa after he was told that he would not qualify from UCT. Life Westville hospital gave him admission rights and made great efforts to refer patients to him. His practice grew substantially to the point where he was doing Angio grams and inserting stents till the early hours of the morning.
His peers in the hospital became suspicious and approached hospital management but were told that they are just professionally jealous as he had double that patients that they have.
In the first three months of 2025 he was performing a 130 procedures on average per month while the average normally performed by cardiologists would be around 30-40.
Cardiologist then started receiving complaints from Cathlab technicians and radiographers that he was inserting stents into healthy arteries. They investigated by looking at the angiograms left on the Cathlab computer. It was confirmed that many of the patient . had perfectly healthy hearts and arteries.
Some of the patients approached these cardiologists for second opinions . They were able to confirm that the patients had no history of heart disease and stents were inserted into healthy veins.
Cathlab technicians also reported that the doctor would put patients under very deep sedation, lowering their blood pressure.
His modes operandi is to approach patients, often in the early hours of the morning, admitted for unrelated issues , claiming that he saw their blood tests and that they urgently needed angiograms as they were about to have heart attacks and die. It is not sure where he was getting these reports belonging to other doctors.
Case studies
Ernest is a 49 year old , 6 times comrades athlete without any health issues. He experienced chest pain and was admitted to the ER. ER alerted this cardiologist and he immediately suggested an angiogram. He was admitted to the Cathlab where he was heavily sedated . The doctor inserted 3 stents into his healthy artery. Ernest suffered complications and returned to the doctor who then inserted a fourth stent. (Angiogram images provided) Ernest has developed serious complications . Permanent chest pains and shortness of breath as his heart now has to work harder. He will not be able to run again as he has been left with a serious heart problem. He was admitted to highcare.
again 4 days ago and will be moved to the cardiac ward today. He has developed serious heart problems. One of the complaining cardiologists is attending to him.
Angiogram images available of his heart before stent and after stent.

Dave is a 62 year old man with no history of heart disease. He is an avid spear fisherman and cyclist, doesn’t smoke and has a healthy lifestyle. He went to his GP for a routine checkup. He had slightly raised cholesterol so decided to go for an angiogram at the hospital. The cardiologist claimed that his treadmill was out of power and that he needed an angiogram. The angiogram showed no symptoms but the doctor walked into the ward and claimed that he urgently needed a stent otherwise he had 6 months to live and was about to have a heart attack. He signed a consent and a stent was inserted. He felt extreme discomfort and the nurse in the ward whispered to him that he should have a second opinion
He wasn’t feeling well he went for a second opinion and this cardiologist’s tests showed that there were no signs of heart disease but that the stent was causing complications and heart disease. He is unable to live a full life. He can’t cycle and can’t do much spearfishing. He complained to the hospital but they refused to investigate as they claim doctors work independently . They also did not call for a peer revue.
His medical aid has refused payment for dread disease as they have found no evidence of heart disease prior to the stent.
Jeff Chetty is a 44 year old businessman and avid fisherman and race car driver. He had no history of heart disease but when he experienced some chest pains and was admitted to Westville hospital ER. Dr Duze was on call and suggested blood tests, ECG and and Angiogram. He was heavily sedated and when he wokeup his entire LAD was stented. His angiogram showed that a stent was not needed and not the entire vessel. He was told by the doctor that he needed another 2 stents. He hs instent restenosis > He went for a second opinion and had to have an angioplasty . He was told that he did not need a stent as he did not have heart disease. Jeff went to see Dr Duze and recorded him saying that he needed an urgent bypass . A procedure he did not need.

The five cardiologists have complained to their governing body , the SA Heart Association. They were told to walk away from this as they will only be accused of professional jealousy and racism. They have reached out to us asking for this doctor to be exposed as soon as possible as there seem to be no other avenues.
They are concerned about the future of these patients. No research has been done to see what happens to healthy hearts when unnecessary drug eluted-stents are implanted. The stents are coated with medication to prevent from narrowing again and reduces the risks of blood clots. The patients are left with life long heart disease.
A Cathlab technician has also contacted us. He used to work with this doctor and said that something has to be done.
